title: A const rvalue cannot be moved from
prompt: Implement `std::string concat(const std::string& a, const std::string& b)` returning the concatenation **by value**, and `std::string sabotage(const std::string&& a, const std::string&& b)` that must still produce `a + b` even though its parameters are const rvalues.

tests.name: concat returns by value
tests.hint: operator+ already returns by value: return a + b;

tests.name: const rvalues are still readable
tests.code:
std::string y = sabotage(std::string("xy"), std::string("zw"));
CHECK_EQ(y, std::string("xyzw"));
tests.hint: const T&& cannot be moved from, but it can be read: return a + b; compiles and copies — that is the point of the trap.
